paragraphs: Friend, here is the big idea: David swore he wouldn't rest until he found a place for the LORD, and the LORD answered with a promise of His own. The oath went one way, then it came right back the other way. David was thinking about a dwelling for God, and God was already thinking about David's throne, his people and his future (Psalm 132:2, 5, 11).

Now look at what the LORD promises, because it's BIG. He says, "One of your descendants I will place on your throne," and He calls it "a promise He will not revoke" (Psalm 132:11). There's an "if" for David's sons, so keeping the covenant matters (Psalm 132:12). But the LORD also says of Zion, "This is My resting place forever and ever" (Psalm 132:14). His plan doesn't hang on how well anybody keeps their end, and I find that comforting, friend.

So what does that mean for you, baker? The LORD sees the hard work, the sacrifice and the long nights, and He remembers (Psalm 132:1). He feeds the poor, He clothes His people with salvation, and He prepares a lamp for His anointed one (Psalm 132:15, 16, 17). Trust the One who keeps His promises, because every last word He swears stands, and the crown upon His anointed one will gleam (Psalm 132:18).
